title: Runtime Kernel Recommender with Warm-Start Fingerprinting
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We see per-model and per-workload variation in best-performing kernel implementations across hardware. Current static rules are overly conservative for mixed seqlen workloads and lead to higher per-token cost or missed latency SLOs for tail requests.

Goal: Build a lightweight runtime recommender that warm-starts from an offline profile database, performs a brief online microprofile for new model/hardware pairs, and adaptively switches kernels at decode-time when workload characteristics change (e.g., sudden seqlen shift, KV cache miss/fill). The system should minimize profiling overhead and provide safe fallbacks.

Scope: prototype and vetted rollout for open models (decoder-only and encoder-decoder) on GPU fleets in Dedicated and Hosted modes. Focus on kernel choices for attention (flash/fused attention, blockwise/fp16 fused matmul kernels), prefill vs decode scheduling, and KV cache-friendly shims.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Profiler runs add no more than 8% median latency overhead on cold-start flows and finish within first 50 requests; 2) For a set of 8 representative models and 3 hardware classes, recommender reduces cost-per-token by >= 6% vs current static policy while keeping P95 latency within SLO; 3) Safe fallback path exists and is exercised in canary runs; 4) Metrics and dashboard for per-model kernel-choice, selection confidence, and A/B delta are instrumented.
updates: 2025-11-12: Ticket created. Initial problem statement and high-level plan. Linked to runtime-autotune initiative.

2025-11-18: Spike completed — small offline profiler (50 warmup samples) identifies that flash-attention wins for seqlen <= 512 on A100 for most decoder models but loses on long seqlen tails; added warm-start idea to seed online bandit with offline priors.

2025-11-25: Design review with Research and Serving teams. Decided on a two-stage approach: offline artifact store + lightweight online microprofile + bandit-based cost model. Action: Marco to draft RFC; Aisha to prototype microprofiler harness.

2025-11-28: Prototype microprofiler landed in a feature branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2146. Early results show 7-9% cost improvement on average for selected models but 12% overhead when naive synchronous profiling used — switching to async background profiling reduces overhead to target.

2025-12-01: Security review pre-check: no secrets required for profiling. Note: telemetry includes kernel choice and timing; added opt-out flag for customer Private deployments. Follow-up: add KMS/HSM-compatible telemetry redaction for Private installs.

2025-12-02: Started canary rollout to 5% of Hosted traffic for the bert-family and a small decoder-only cohort. Grafana dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rt-kernel-recs/perf?orgId=1 (internal).
implementation_notes:
Core components: (1) offline profile DB keyed by model fingerprint + hardware fingerprint; (2) microprofiler that runs 3 prioritized kernel variants asynchronously on warm-start requests and records latency/cost; (3) online bandit cost model (Thompson sampling) that merges offline priors with online evidence; (4) runtime hook that can switch kernel selection at prefill vs decode boundaries and when seqlen distribution shifts above thresholds; (5) safety layer: guardrails that revert to baseline when confidence low or when observed P95 regresses.

Telemetry: emit per-request kernel_id, seqlen, batch_size, latency, token_count, cost_estimate, profile_phase. Implement sampling at 5% for verbose traces to limit overhead.

Rollout: unit tests -> perf harness -> shadow experiments -> 5% canary -> 25% -> full.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Profiling overhead adding tail latency for first requests. Mitigation: run profiler async and return baseline kernel for first response; apply hedged request for high-priority traffic.
Risk: Oscillation between kernels causing cache churn. Mitigation: hysteresis (min dwell time), require statistically significant evidence before switch, and prefer decode-safe kernels when KV hit ratio low.
Risk: Inconsistent results across hardware driver versions. Mitigation: include driver/driver-build in hardware fingerprint and invalidate offline priors when driver mismatch exceeds threshold.
testing_plan: 1) Microbench harness that runs candidate kernels across seqlen sweep and batch sizes, reports per-kernel latency distribution. 2) Integration test in staging with synthetic seqlen spikes. 3) Canary on small percentage of hosted traffic with automated rollback on perf regressions. 4) Long-running A/B on Dedicated with billing comparison and qualitative output parity checks.
deliverables: Migration playbook: steps to enable/disable per-deployment
notes_for_reviewers: Pay attention to the safety layer and the explicit thresholds for switching. We intentionally limit synchronous profiling to avoid cold-start regressions; reviewers should validate the math behind Thompson sampling priors and the observable feature set used for fingerprints (model_arch, param_count, layer_types, kv-cache-behavior, driver_version).
